cli.classify_project_scope.description:
classify-project-scope.py - bring one project's memory in line with the scope layering rules.

Rules (TECH.md section 4.4): personal is for the author only; a project rule is not a personal preference, so it goes to shared with the proposer recorded as Author; the index scope is derived from the path; atoms of other projects are not injected. The work is split in two:
  what a script can decide (write index scope back, dangling entries, Scope/Author headers, moving files, regenerating directories) -> this tool does it;
  what needs a human (for each personal atom: move to shared / keep personal / make cross-project / delete) -> this tool first gives a suggestion table,
  Claude Code asks the user, and after the decision runs `apply`.

Usage (run at the project root, or pass --memory-dir <proj>/.claude/memory):
  status                         organized yet? (_atom_index.json.layout=="scope-v2" or shared/_taxonomy.json)
  plan                           JSON: a suggestion per personal atom (shared / personal / review = looks project-specific, needs a human) + index problem counts + number of flat shared atoms
  apply --decisions <file.json>  {slug: "shared"|"personal"|"cross_project"|"reject"}; unlisted atoms are left alone; runs mark when done
  mark                           only set the "organized" marker

cli.cleanup_projects_residue.description:
cleanup-projects-residue.py - clean up leftovers in ~/.claude/projects/{slug}/memory/

Project-layer memory lives in {project_root}/.claude/memory/; ~/.claude/projects/{slug}/memory/ is left as a migration stub or an empty shell, which pollutes:
  - the audit's cross-layer duplicate detection
  - the double .claude layer (trigger of the P1 hole)
  - the vector indexer's layer enumeration

Strategy: archive (mv into _archive/), never delete; can be moved back any time.

Usage:
    python cleanup-projects-residue.py              # dry-run, only lists the plan
    python cleanup-projects-residue.py --apply      # actually archive
    python cleanup-projects-residue.py --restore    # restore from the latest archive (emergency)

# What this directory is

The project layer of Claude Code "atom memory". The decisions and pitfalls of this project are written as memory cards and stored in `shared/` and `failures/`, version-controlled with the project and shared with all teammates.

# How to connect

After the root layer is installed, pulling this project connects it automatically; no extra setup is needed. For install steps see Install.md in the root-layer repo: <root-layer repo URL>

# Note

Do not hand-edit `_atom_index.json`: it is an index the system derives from the cards (already in `.gitignore`), and hand edits will be overwritten.

eval_usage.py - evaluate detect_atom_use (the "was this atom used this round" judgement of usefulness attribution) against a labelled set.

cli.move_dir_check.epilog:
move-dir-check.py - the two receipts after moving a code directory (rule MOVE_CODE_DIR_NEEDS_SCAN_AND_SAMPLE, hooks/wg_release_rules.py).

What it does:
  scan    search the whole repo for the old path string (absolute, relative, forward and back slashes all count) and print the hits; last line `MOVE_PATH_SCAN DONE hits=<n>`.
          Fix the code and rescan until 0 hits; exclude deliberate leftovers (e.g. a changelog) with --allow; the command itself is the record of what was kept.
  sample  --for names which new directory this sampling covers (closing only settles the moves that are named), and runs the sampling check you choose (--run, e.g. an import smoke test of the moved Python module or the target verify); for C# add --csproj-check <new dir> to check that every .cs inside is compiled by some .csproj (SDK style by default includes everything under the project directory, or an explicit Compile Include), and when there is a .sln that .csproj must be listed in it. All passing ends with
          `MOVE_SAMPLE_CHECK PASS`, otherwise `MOVE_SAMPLE_CHECK FAIL` (exit 1).

How to run (at the project root; otherwise add --root <project root>):
  {cmd} scan --old lib/pkg --new src/pkg [--allow CHANGELOG.md]
  {cmd} sample --for src/pkg --run "python -c "import src.pkg"" [--csproj-check src/pkg]
See --help for all options.

cli.overview_map_scaffold.description:
overview-map-scaffold.py: scan a project from scratch into a parts-map skeleton plus five-section placeholder cards; reconcile the map and cards (G14).

What it does: scans the top-level directories of `--cwd` as parts, puts fix hotspots first, writes one [tentative] skeleton card per row, and produces `<project>/.claude/overview-map.md`.
Dry-run by default: only decides card names and pre-validates each card, writes nothing; `--write` writes: card by card, and the map only after all cards exist; if any card fails it stops at once, writes no map, deletes nothing, exit 1 (stderr lists written / failed / unwritten); rerunning the same command reuses the cards already written (a card is reused only if its part line matches or its Source is a scaffold product, and its entry in _atom_index.json is checked and filled in if missing; a same-named hand-written card -> stop and ask you to rename or delete) and finishes the rest.
An existing map is always refused; `--merge-missing` pairs by the existing map's prefix -> card name and only adds missing rows and cards whose file is missing though the map has the row.
The layer the cards go to is detected automatically: ~/.claude -> root layer (global + realm local + MemDev); organization root -> organization layer; anything else -> project shared.
A root-layer worktree (a git worktree of this live repo) counts as root layer and reads cards from the worktree's own memory / _AIDocs/_atoms; `--write` is always refused there (exit 2).

How to run:
  {cmd} --cwd <project root>                 # preview (writes nothing)
  {cmd} --cwd <project root> --write         # write map + cards
  {cmd} --cwd <project root> --write --merge-missing   # only add directories missing from the map
  {cmd} check --cwd <project root>           # map/card reconciliation
Last line: scan `OVERVIEW_SCAFFOLD DONE rows=<n>`; reconcile `OVERVIEW_SCAFFOLD CHECK PASS|FAIL issues=<n>`.
exit: 0 done; 1 reconciliation problems or a card failed to write (map not written, written cards kept); 2 argument / Lv1 / root directory error; 3 map exists and was refused.
Settings: `overview_scaffold` (scaffold_ignore, layers, scaffold_default_lv1) and `refix_churn` (refix_*) in `workflow/config.json`.
See --help for all options.
